title: fix(plugin-form): warn on an unresolvable top-level `fields` member (route 1)
body:
Fixes objectstack-ai/objectui#8738
Refs objectstack-ai/objectui#8847

## What

Route 1 of #8738 (ruled at issuecomment-5603577602, after route 2 landed as #8846): a top-level `fields` member that resolves to no name now fires a **named `console.warn`** instead of vanishing in total silence.

- `sectionFields.ts`: new exported `warnUnresolvedTopLevelField(entry, objectName)`, right beside its existing sibling `warnOnMixedVocabulary` — same voice, same once-per-occurrence dedupe discipline (a module-level `Set` keyed by object + skipped shape). It only warns; it never resolves a name from `entry` — no `?? f.field` fallback, per the card's own standing prohibition.
- Wired into **both** read paths named in the ruling:
  - `ObjectForm.tsx`'s `SimpleObjectForm` `fieldsToShow` loop.
  - `flatFields.ts`'s `buildFlatFields` (the drawer/modal path, identical shape).
- Message names the skipped shape (`{ field: 'note' }`) and the vocabulary difference (`sections[].fields` accepts the spec `FormFieldSchema` object, identity key `field`; top-level `fields` takes bare names only).

### #8847 — measured, not assumed

Re-derived on this branch's base (`42df92809`, post-#8846):

```
:232  object-form                { name: 'fields', ..., description: '...' }      ← described (#8846)
:292  form / view:form           { name: 'fields', type: 'array' }                ← bare (fixed here)
:430  object-master-detail-form  { name: 'fields', ..., description: '...' }      ← described but doesn't mention the trap (extended here)
```

(Note: the claim comment's `:346` for `object-master-detail-form` was stale on this tree — line 346 is `embeddable-form`'s `fields`, not master-detail's. Re-derived directly against `index.tsx` on `origin/main`; see the report's `out_of_scope_findings` for that third surface.)

**Coverage measured, both surfaces inherit route 1 for free:**
- `form` / `view:form` is registered on the *exact same* `ObjectFormRenderer` component as `object-form` — same code path by construction, not merely similar.
- `object-master-detail-form`'s parent `fields` (no `sections`) is passed straight through `MasterDetailForm`'s `parentSchema` into `<ObjectForm>`; every sectioned branch in `ObjectForm.tsx`'s formType routing guards on `schema.sections?.length`, so a fields-only parent always falls through to `SimpleObjectForm` regardless of `formType`. New pin: `__tests__/topLevelFieldsWarnCoverage-8847.test.tsx`, rendering `MasterDetailForm` directly and asserting the warning fires (and does not fire for a legal bare name — the firing control).

⇒ #8847's remaining work was documentation-only for both surfaces, closed here by extending/adding their registration `description`. Left as `Refs` (not `Fixes`) since the closing decision belongs to whoever reviews the measurement, but from this seat both halves are closed.

## Existing probe (objectFormFieldsMembers-8071.test.tsx) — ran first, one assertion moved, on purpose

Ran unmodified against the new source change before touching the test file:

```
Test Files  1 failed (1)
     Tests  1 failed | 5 passed (6)
```

The **only** failure was row 4's `expect(warn).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` — which encoded the PRE-route-1 silence for the exact `{ field: 'note' }` input the ruling requires to warn on. Rows 1/2/3/5/6 (all render-output assertions) were untouched. This is not "changed behaviour beyond a warning" — the render outcome in row 4 (`toEqual([])`) is byte-for-bit identical; only the "no warning happened" assumption is falsified, along exactly the axis the ruling changed on purpose.

Resolution: updated row 4 to assert the warning fires with the expected content (kept the render assertion), updated its title/comment and the file's top docblock (which also said "no console warning"), and added a **new pin** below row 6 with route 1's required firing control (fires for an unresolvable member, does not fire for a legal bare name) — mirrored in `flatFields.test.ts` for the drawer/modal path.

Re-ran after the test-file edit:
```
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  8 passed (8)
```
